$comment: Dev bench scenarios (docs/DEV_TOOLS.md; scripts/scenarios.ts describes the steps, scripts/bench.ts runs them). Each runs in a fresh local world: the player at the spawn, then the steps in order.

scenarios.name: idle-spawn
scenarios.notes: Standing at the spawn looking at the horizon once the LOD has loaded: the steady-state frame.

scenarios.name: fly-low-fast
scenarios.notes: Flying fast (level 6, at least 88 m/s) about 15 m over the terrain (owner, 2026-10-14: the hitch seen when flying low): full-detail chunks streaming in as fast as the player moves. Heading +X (yaw 90) from the seed-7 spawn: a clear 1.7 km (flying is stopped by any ledge it hits: low enough to stream full-detail chunks, high enough not to snag).

scenarios.name: fly-low-faster
scenarios.notes: Flying fast (level 8, at least 176 m/s) about 15 m over the terrain (owner, 2026-10-14: the hitch seen when flying low): full-detail chunks streaming in as fast as the player moves. Heading +X (yaw 90) from the seed-7 spawn: a clear 1.7 km (flying is stopped by any ledge it hits: low enough to stream full-detail chunks, high enough not to snag).

scenarios.name: jump-onto-block
scenarios.notes: Places a block in front of the spawn, walks into it and jumps with forward held (owner, 2026-10-14: the jump usually failed to clear one block): the player should land on top (grounded 1 m up), then walk off its far side.

scenarios.name: water-views
scenarios.notes: The sea seen four ways (Phase 26 W1b, the water shader): flies from the seed-7 spawn to the coast about 20 km east-south-east (yaw 112.5) and down into the sea, then places the camera around the player, where the chunks are streamed: across the sea at a low angle, down into the shallows toward the coast, from 1 km up, and with the eye just under the surface (the underwater stub). Records the frame over the sea.

scenarios.name: water-shore
scenarios.notes: The shore in the water's depth views (Phase 26 W3): flies to the water-views coast, then shoots the beach edge at a low angle, straight down into the shallows over sand, the deep-to-shallow gradient from 20 m up, under the surface in the shallows (the floor and its caustics, along it, up toward the surface) and the far water from 1 km.

scenarios.name: water-reflections
scenarios.notes: The water's reflections (Phase 26 W5a: land by screen-space reflection, clouds along the reflected ray) on Medium: flies to the water-views coast, then from 1.5 m over a lagoon shoots a sand bank and the treeline behind it at a low angle (recorded: the cost), turned and steeper, the beach across open water at several pitches and from the side (the screen-edge fades), the clouds in the sea, then the bank at dusk and at night and the low sun over the water.

scenarios.name: jump-in-place
scenarios.notes: Jumps on flat ground at the spawn: the controller trace shows the jump's peak.

scenarios.name: look-horizon
scenarios.notes: From the player's eyes at the spawn, looking along the ground 3° below the horizon (heading +X): grazing rays, a ray marcher's worst case (docs/RAY_MARCHED_RENDERER.md §5).

scenarios.name: look-down
scenarios.notes: From the player's eyes at the spawn, looking 80° down at the ground: short rays, a ray marcher's best case.

scenarios.name: edit-burst
scenarios.notes: Places and breaks a block in front of the spawn 150 times each (300 edits, about one per 0.12 s, just over the edit interval): the cost of remeshing and uploading edited chunks.

scenarios.name: fly-high
scenarios.notes: Flies up about 540 m (level 8 for 3 s), looks out and down 20° and flies +X for 10 s: far terrain, the LOD's distant levels streaming.

scenarios.name: thermal-10min
scenarios.notes: Phone-oriented: ten minutes of flight 60 m up at level 4 (at least 44 m/s) round a 660 m square, for thermal throttling: the last minute's frame intervals against the first's. Run it on a phone (or with the device's own heat in mind); it takes over ten minutes.

scenarios.name: day-night
scenarios.notes: The day/night cycle (docs/DAY_NIGHT.md): from 2 s of flight above the seed-7 spawn, each time of day looking toward the sun (or the moon by night) and away from it, then the moon at three phases.

scenarios.name: day-timelapse
scenarios.notes: A whole day in 48 frames looking along the sun's path toward sunset (yaw -150), from above the spawn.

scenarios.name: day-night-cost
scenarios.notes: The day/night cycle's GPU cost (run with --unthrottled; clouds off, so the sky is the cycle alone): the spawn view at noon and at midnight (the stars drawn), and looking up into the sky at both.

scenarios.name: sprint-straight
scenarios.notes: Sprints (Shift + W) along +X from the seed-7 spawn (Phase 29 motion effects): the FOV widens by the sprint boost and faint wind streaks show at the screen's edges; a shot standing, mid-sprint, then standing again.

scenarios.name: fly-fast-turn
scenarios.notes: Flies fast (level 8 with Run: the terrain band's 400 m/s cap) from the seed-7 spawn, then turns and dives (Phase 29 motion effects): the strong flight streaks, and the vanishing point following the direction of travel as the view turns away from it.

scenarios.name: clouds-high
scenarios.notes: The sky's clouds on High (docs/CLOUDS.md): shots looking up, at the horizon and toward the sun, then 5 s recorded looking 25° up (mostly sky). Run with --unthrottled to compare gpu.composite between clouds-high, clouds-low and clouds-off.

scenarios.name: clouds-low
scenarios.notes: clouds-high on Low (fewer octaves, no self-shadow).

scenarios.name: clouds-off
scenarios.notes: clouds-high with the clouds off: the baseline for their GPU cost.

scenarios.name: clouds-night
scenarios.notes: The clouds by moonlight (midnight).

scenarios.name: clouds-dusk
scenarios.notes: The clouds with a low sun (golden hour, the sun about 5° up toward yaw −152), toward it and away.

scenarios.name: clouds-fly
scenarios.notes: Flying fast (level 10, at least 352 m/s) climbing toward the cloud deck: the clouds move past with parallax and drift; shots every few seconds, the last looking up from near the deck as the clouds fade.

scenarios.name: clouds-altitude
scenarios.notes: The camera placed 1000 m, 1500 m and 1700 m up (the deck is at 1800 m): the clouds come nearer and larger, then fade out as the eye reaches the deck.

scenarios.name: day-night-face-b
scenarios.notes: The day/night cycle on face B (DAY_NIGHT.md §3): a camera 50 m over face B's sea; face A's noon is face B's midnight (the moon overhead), face A's sunset is face B's sunrise.

scenarios.name: clouds-above
scenarios.notes: The cloud deck (1.8 km up) seen from above (CLOUDS.md §7): the camera 3.5 km up looking down at 40°, then 15 km up (a cloud sea to the deck's horizon), then 5 s recorded 3.5 km up looking down (the deck over the terrain: compare gpu.composite with clouds-off).

scenarios.name: clouds-above-off
scenarios.notes: clouds-above's recorded view with the clouds off: the baseline for the deck's cost from above.

scenarios.name: clouds-through
scenarios.notes: Rising through the deck (1.8 km): the camera at 1.3, 1.65, 1.8, 1.95 and 2.3 km looking 10° down: the deck fades out below it, the in-cloud fog where a cloud is, then the deck's top below. No pop between the shots. At the deck's height also at x = 1.5, 3, 4.5 and 6 km, so some shots are inside a cloud (the in-cloud fog).

scenarios.name: clouds-level
scenarios.notes: At the deck's height (1.8 km) looking at the horizon, and 100 m above and below it.

scenarios.name: clouds-above-night
scenarios.notes: The deck from above by moonlight (midnight), 3.5 km up looking down at 30°.

scenarios.name: walk-over-a-placed-block
scenarios.notes: Places a block in front of the spawn and walks over it without jumping (Phase 18, ADAPTIVE_BLOCKS.md): natural ground shapes itself, so the placed block is a half pyramid (45° faces: a slide, owner 2026-10-15) and the ground under and around it ramps up at 27° — the controller trace shows what the player does on it (no jump, no launch).

scenarios.name: slide-off-a-steep-block
scenarios.notes: Slides on 45° ground (PLAYER_CONTROLLER.md §6.8, owner 2026-10-15): places a block in front of the spawn (natural ground shapes it into a half pyramid with 45° faces), walks up the 27° ground around it into its 45° face (walking up it fails: the player slides back, braking), steers right along the face mid-slide with forward still held, then lets go and slides off. The controller trace (records.slide.ticks) shows the Sliding state, the speeds and the steer; the sounds (window.__dwell.sounds) the slide's loop and stop.

scenarios.name: sprint-slide
scenarios.notes: The sprint slide (PLAYER_CONTROLLER.md §6.9, owner 2026-10-19): sprints (Shift+W), presses crouch (C) to slide on in the crouch capsule, steers right (D) mid-slide, jumps out (Space) keeping the momentum; then, crouch let go, sprints and slides again after the cooldown and rides it out to the crouch speed. Screenshots through the slide (the lower eye, the FOV widening); the controller trace (records.slide.ticks) shows the Sliding state, the crouch flag, the speed falling with friction and the jump; the sounds the crouch and the slide's scrape.

scenarios.name: slopes-near-far
scenarios.notes: Natural slopes from the player's eyes, looking down at the ground nearby and out to the horizon (Phase 18): screenshots of the adaptive shapes near (chunks) and far (the LOD's sloped tops), and the steady frame there.

scenarios.name: spyglass-far
scenarios.notes: The spyglass (docs/SPYGLASS.md): flies about 180 m up over the seed-7 spawn and looks out over the distant terrain 6° down (heading +X), then shoots it unzoomed, zoomed to each step once the LOD has refined inside the narrow view, and unzoomed again. Run it with --compare (or a scenario per renderer) to see the ray marcher's and the LOD's far detail side by side.
